Actual inspected pixels: Motivation: compact features support localization, grasping and navigation. Raw-pixel impossibility is overbroad; learned systems can learn their own features. Counts are illustrative.
Why Feature Extraction Matters in Robotics

•  A camera frame contains millions of raw pixel values. A robot cannot plan,
   navigate, or grasp using raw pixels directly — it needs compact, meaningful,
   repeatable descriptions of what it sees.
•  Reduces Dimensionality
    –  Millions of pixels → a few hundred informative numbers.
•  Enables Localization
    –  Distinctive points let a robot recognize 'where am I’.
•  Drives Manipulation
    – Edges & corners locate object boundaries for grasping.
•  Supports Navigation
    –  Obstacle and lane features guide path planning.

•  Information lost in pixel-to-feature conversion is
   compensated using scene-based assumptions based on

Summary

•  Image features reduce raw pixel data into useful information for recognition,
   tracking, and motion analysis.
•  Feature extraction depends on assumptions about lighting, visibility, and scene
   conditions, making it imperfect.
•  Features are classified into region, line, and point features for analyzing objects,
   edges, and keypoints.
•  Region features use thresholding, clustering, segmentation, and descriptors like
  moments and circularity for object analysis.
•  Line features use gradients, Canny edge detection, and the
   Hough Transform to detect edges and straight lines.
•  Point features such as Harris corners and SIFT provide

concepts.title: Task-relevant compression
concepts.description: Features summarize selected structure, such as corners or boundaries, rather than guaranteeing lossless reconstruction or universally sufficient information.

concepts.title: Explicit versus learned representations
concepts.description: The lecture motivates extracting informative representations. It does not establish that explicit hand-engineered feature extraction is a universal prerequisite for every pixel-input model.

concepts.title: Feature output diagram
concepts.description: The diagram separates several useful representations; it does not say that a single still image alone supplies unambiguous physical velocity.

concepts.title: Perspective and physical size
concepts.description: The near cube projects larger than the far cube. Metric size cannot generally be recovered from pixel count alone.

concepts.title: Assumption failures
concepts.description: Visible image evidence may omit hidden object parts and may change with illumination, shadows or reflections. These effects constrain feature reliability.

concepts.title: Region, line and point features
concepts.description: Region features summarize connected appearance, line features represent straight geometry, and point features identify distinctive locations.

concepts.title: Segmentation and robustness
concepts.description: The sign mask separates foreground structures from the background. Semantic recognition is a separate task, and robustness is bounded by available evidence.

concepts.title: Three stages of region features
concepts.description: Classification gives pixel classes; instance segmentation distinguishes connected objects; description measures their properties.

concepts.title: Otsu objective
concepts.description: Otsu chooses a global histogram threshold using the weighted variance separation criterion, not a prescribed class proportion.

concepts.title: Adaptive threshold calculation
concepts.description: The threshold is 110 intensity units, and the specified comparison classifies 115 as foreground.

concepts.title: Primaries and optical path
concepts.description: The page lists the three wavelength values and depicts illuminant, reflecting object and eye. The separate attribution of all three wavelengths to mercury lines is not used as a factual premise.

concepts.title: XYZ and perceptual distance
concepts.description: The page motivates XYZ coordinates and approximate perceptual uniformity in CIELAB; neither is a guarantee of complete appearance invariance.

concepts.title: Two-dimensional chromaticity

concepts.title: Chromatic segmentation
concepts.description: L* represents lightness and a*,b* the opponent chromatic coordinates. Removing L* changes the metric used for clustering but does not make k-means parameter-free or universally illumination-invariant.

concepts.title: Lab chromatic axes

concepts.title: Classes versus objects
concepts.description: The four yellow regions can share one chromatic class, with background forming the other. Class labels and instance labels answer different questions.

concepts.title: Color-space centroids
concepts.description: Color-cluster centers summarize appearance. They are distinct from the spatial centroids computed after instance segmentation.

concepts.title: Cluster labels and plotting colors
concepts.description: The inspected result uses a colormap for integer classes. The source mapping is particular to this example, not a semantic guarantee for every run.

concepts.title: Binary foreground conversion

concepts.title: Connected-component count convention

concepts.title: Connectivity changes instances
concepts.description: Instance segmentation depends on the neighborhood convention. This declared two-pixel example makes the difference explicit.

concepts.title: Binary versus weighted moments
concepts.description: The area-as-count interpretation assumes a binary 0/1 mask. Other weights produce weighted moments.

concepts.title: Centroid from raw moments
concepts.description: The first moments divided by area give the average foreground coordinate.

concepts.title: Moment order and translation
concepts.description: Raw moment order is the sum of its exponents. Central moments describe the distribution around its centroid.

concepts.title: Central second-moment calculation
concepts.description: The central identities subtract centroid-dependent terms from the raw moments.

concepts.title: Equivalent ellipse semiaxes
concepts.description: The source expression gives semiaxes of the equal-moment filled ellipse. Its minor-to-major ratio is 0.5.

concepts.title: Moment-to-orientation synthesis
concepts.description: Solving det(J−λI)=0 gives (5−λ)²−4=0, hence λ=7,3. The major eigendirection is (1,1), modulo its sign. With m00=4, the semiaxes are √7 and √3.

concepts.title: Orientation ambiguity
concepts.description: A robust interpretation uses atan2(v_y,v_x), treats opposite vectors as the same axis and recognizes isotropic degeneracy.

concepts.title: Hu moment invariance
concepts.description: Hu invariants use normalized central moments, not merely arbitrary unnormalized moments. Sampling and numerical precision affect practical invariance.

concepts.title: Connected labels versus blob indices
concepts.description: Class IDs, connected labels and blob-list indices are distinct conventions. The top target’s correspondence is established by its position.

concepts.title: Fractional area qualification
concepts.description: The blob API derives shape measurements from contours. Its continuous polygon area can have half-unit values, unlike a direct integer pixel sum.

concepts.title: Boundary chain code
concepts.description: Direction codes compactly encode a boundary path. Metric length depends on step geometry, while the initial pixel fixes its translation.

concepts.title: Circle and square circularity
concepts.description: For a circle A=πr²,P=2πr; for a square A=s²,P=4s. The resulting ratios are 1 and π/4.

concepts.title: Circularity under resizing
concepts.description: Circularity is dimensionless and scale invariant in the ideal model; finite raster estimates can differ after resampling.

concepts.title: Radius signature and rotation

concepts.title: Polar profile index mismatch

concepts.title: Normalized radius and polar matching
concepts.description: Radius normalization preserves relative shape variation. Profile matching can estimate a rotational offset; the function argument identifies the comparison target.

concepts.title: Perimeter samples versus length
concepts.description: The contour contains coordinate samples, conventionally one point per column, while perimeter_length measures distances along the boundary.

concepts.title: Detection versus instance masks

concepts.title: Training-set class scope

concepts.title: Line feature utility
concepts.description: Straight boundaries are useful geometric features in many engineered environments, without implying all scenes or all useful boundaries are straight.

concepts.title: Gradient magnitude and direction
concepts.description: The theory slide uses √(I_u²+I_v²) and atan2(I_v,I_u).

concepts.title: Smoothing and derivative convolution
concepts.description: Associativity combines the filters in the ideal or consistently handled convolution model; implementation boundaries remain relevant.

concepts.title: Canny nonmaximum suppression
concepts.description: Nonmaximum suppression retains local ridge peaks along the gradient direction, making the edge response thin.

concepts.title: Canny hysteresis reasoning
concepts.description: Hysteresis retains weak responses that are connected to strong evidence, not every response above the low threshold.

concepts.title: Hough polar parameters
concepts.description: The polar representation avoids an infinite-slope special case by using a normal angle and perpendicular offset.

concepts.title: Vertical line in Hough coordinates
concepts.description: The equation reduces to ρ=u=6 for all points on the vertical line.

concepts.title: Accumulator voting
concepts.description: A peak indicates support shared by multiple image points, subject to discretization and threshold choices.

concepts.title: Five-point line support
concepts.description: The diagonal contains (39,9),(24,24),(9,39), while the lower horizontal contains (9,39),(39,39). Coordinates are an explicitly declared idealization of the figure.

concepts.title: Church edge-to-line pipeline
concepts.description: The code smooths the grayscale input, computes an edge map and detects line segments supported by those edges.

concepts.title: Line segment parameter roles
concepts.description: The HoughP arguments constrain segment length and allowed interruption. They do not promise an exact number of returned lines.

concepts.title: Theory versus Canny default
concepts.description: The mathematical presentation and the displayed API defaults are not identical. State the norm explicitly when reproducing numerical behavior.

concepts.title: Harris window matrix
concepts.description: Image derivatives may be computed by derivative-of-Gaussian filtering, but the structure matrix is built from the resulting image-gradient products.

concepts.title: Flat, edge and corner cases
concepts.description: A corner produces significant variation in both local directions, unlike a flat region or one dominant edge.

concepts.title: Harris response calculation
concepts.description: The determinant is 16 and the trace is 8, so the response is 16−2.56=13.44.

concepts.title: Harris scale qualification
concepts.description: Harris corners at a fixed scale can disappear or change character when the image scale changes. SIFT incorporates characteristic-scale selection.

concepts.title: Difference of Gaussians
concepts.description: Subtracting nearby Gaussian scale levels approximates a proportional scale-normalized LoG response, which motivates efficient scale-space extrema detection.

concepts.title: Scale-space extrema neighborhood
concepts.description: The local 3×3×3 neighborhood has 27 samples, one of which is the candidate; 26 remain.

concepts.title: Scale extrema and stability
concepts.description: Scale-space extrema supply candidates, followed by localization and removal of unstable responses.

concepts.title: SIFT pipeline
concepts.description: SIFT finds stable position/scale candidates, assigns local orientation and then describes local image structure.

concepts.title: Descriptor dimensions
concepts.description: The descriptor contains 4×4×8=128 histogram values.

concepts.title: Orientation alignment and bins
concepts.description: A local reference orientation supports rotation robustness; its assignment must not be conflated with the later eight-bin spatial histograms.

concepts.title: Strength filter semantics

concepts.title: Keypoint overlay interpretation
concepts.description: SIFT’s plotted support scale and orientation are feature attributes. They should not be read as object extents or physical units.

concepts.title: Choosing features for a task
concepts.description: The summary combines complementary region, line and point representations. The choice depends on the task, assumptions and the information required.

concepts.title: Hough threshold boundary
